newsitem.title: UK: BG steady after results, focus on MMC.
newsitem.headline: BG steady after results, focus on MMC.

text.p: Shares in gas pipeline operator BG Plc edged up in pre-market trade on Thursday after the group reported higher first-quarter profits, but gains were capped ahead of an upcoming report from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.
The shares rose 1-1/2p to 183p by 0727 GMT.
BG, which was formed by the British Gas demerger in February this year, reported pretax profits of 615 million stg compared with 560 million a year ago.
But analysts said attention remained fixed on a crucial report on proposed price changes from the MMC, which is expected to come out in June.
"The results turned up no surprises," said Nigel Hawkins, industry analyst at Yamaichi.
"The key for BG is the battle for TransCo which overshadows the results," he said.
TransCo, the gas transport operation of British Gas, is the sole dividend source for BG. It contributed 631 million stg to group operating profits.

"The Group will be sustantially affected by the outcome of the MMC Inquiry into the Ofgas proposals for the regulation of TransCo," the company said in its results statement. "This will be the key element in establishing an appropriate level of dividend from BG Plc."
"Under the current Labour government, I think that if BG doesn't do well out of the MMC the government may intervene," Hawkins said.
"They could give big price reductions to customers nationwide and possibly do a deal on the windfall tax as well. The silence is deafening on this," the analyst said.
